transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on glasses usually means dirty water is being sprayed back onto them during the cycle. The most common cause for this in Beko dishwashers is a blocked filter that isn't trapping food properly. Please do these two simple checks:
1. Twist and lift out the main filter at the bottom of the tub, rinse it under a tap, and check if it was clogged with food or grit.
2. Turn each spray arm by hand to make sure it spins freely, and look into the little jet holes on the arms to see if any are blocked by seeds or scale. Let me know what you find with those.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

ok did both. filter was full of food n grease, rinsed it. lower spray arm spins fine but upper one is stiff, and a few holes on it were blocked with seeds/limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick

Good work clearing those jets. Since the arm was stiff before cleaning, and even after clearing the holes it may still feel tight, the issue is likely the bearing or mounting point itself rather than just the blockage. Please remove the upper spray arm completely (it usually unclips or unscrews) and try spinning it by hand again. 1. If it spins freely now, put it back on securely and run a test cycle. 2. If it is still stiff, wobbly, or catches, the mounting bearing is likely worn or there is debris trapped under the arm's base. Let me know if it spins freely once removed.
not sure how to get the upper arm off tbh, didnt try. is it def needed? i did clear the holes so was hoping that was enough

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. If the arm doesn't spin freely, water pressure will be wasted on friction rather than spraying your dishes. Please try this: reach up to where the upper spray arm connects to the tub (you may need to remove the top rack to get a better angle). Pull or twist it gently to detach it from its mounting post. Once it is off, spin the shaft by hand. 1. If it spins freely and smoothly now, put it back on firmly and run a test cycle.
2. If it still feels stiff, loose, or wobbly even when detached, the mounting bearing is likely worn and needs replacing.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok will try taking it off. btw when i said i cleared the holes, ran a normal cycle after and it was much better tbh. is that enough?

Yes, that is absolutely enough. If the cycle ran much better after you cleared those jets and cleaned the filter, then the blockage was the only issue. You don't need to remove or replace any parts. To stop it happening again, just keep an eye on the spray arm holes and give the bottom filter a quick rinse every few weeks if you tend to wash gritty pots.
